title: writeWordEmbedding
summary: Write a word embedding model to a UTF-8 word2vec text file.

gpu_support.notes: `writeWordEmbedding` serializes host wordEmbedding metadata and writes a file; it does not use provider kernels.

description: `writeWordEmbedding(emb, filename)` writes a `wordEmbedding` object to a UTF-8 text file in word2vec text format.
behaviors: `emb` must be a `wordEmbedding` object with `Dimension`, `Vocabulary`, and vector storage created by `readWordEmbedding`, `trainWordEmbedding`, or `fastTextWordEmbedding`.
`filename` may be a string scalar, character vector, or a 1-by-1 cell array containing a character vector.
The output file starts with a `numWords dimension` header followed by one row per vocabulary word and its vector values.
The target file is created or overwritten. Parent directories must already exist.
Vocabulary entries containing whitespace and non-finite vector values are rejected because word2vec text rows cannot represent them unambiguously.
Binary word2vec output, zip output, append mode, and format-selection options are not part of the compatibility target's documented `writeWordEmbedding` syntax and are not accepted.
The filename must be host text. Native integer and resident numeric filename values are rejected before provider or filesystem access.

examples.output: `colors.vec` contains UTF-8 word2vec text embedding data.
`copy` is a `wordEmbedding` object with the same vocabulary and vectors.

faqs.question: What file format does `writeWordEmbedding` use?
faqs.answer: It writes UTF-8 word2vec text format with a header row and one word-vector row per vocabulary entry.

faqs.question: Does `writeWordEmbedding` create folders?
faqs.answer: No. Create the parent folder first with `mkdir` if needed.

faqs.question: Does `writeWordEmbedding` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It is host object serialization and file I/O.

points: `filename` must identify a writable host filesystem path as a scalar text value or 1-by-1 cell containing a character vector.
The output text is UTF-8 and can be read back with `readWordEmbedding`.

gpu_residency: `writeWordEmbedding` is a host file-I/O sink and does not launch provider kernels. Resident numeric filename inputs are rejected rather than gathered because they are not valid paths.
